newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end slightly lower.

text.p: A stronger opening on Wall Street led to a recovery of Swiss shares in late trade, but Swiss indices still ended weaker after Tuesday's record close.

Dealers said worries about a possible U.S. interest rate hike may keep a lid on the market ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting on February 4-5. Interest concentrated on pharmaceuticals Novartis and Roche, which were pressured by profit taking.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended down 12.6 points, or 0.3 percent, to 4,169.7 points.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 10.04 points, or 0.38 percent, to 2,666.63 points.
Roche certificates, which have been in the limelight for the past few sessions due to various merger and spin-off rumours, fell 110 francs, or 0.92 percent, to 11.910.
One dealer said speculation was still a factor in Roche's moves.
Novartis registered shares gave up nine francs to 1,605.
Sulzer registereds stood out with a surge of 25 francs to 960 on speculation the company may be planning a single share structure. Sulzer denied there were any plans to do so.
ABB, Ems-Chemie, CS Group, SBC, Zurich and Swissair were among the winners.
UBS bearers ended 12 francs lower at 1,183.
